# Samuṭṭhānavāra (Pvr 1.13)

**ID:** Pvr 1.13
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Samuṭṭhānavāra
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuṭṭhānavāra* ("Section on Origination") is the thirteenth sub-chapter of the first major division of the *Parivāra* in the Vinaya Piṭaka [Horner 1966]. Functioning as an analytical handbook of monastic discipline, the chapter categorizes ecclesiastical offenses according to their originations (*samuṭṭhāna*), systematically defining transgressions as arising through body (*kāya*), speech (*vācā*), or mind (*citta*). The text also structures offenses according to four permutations of awareness: falling into an offense unconsciously and rising from it consciously, falling into it consciously and rising unconsciously, falling into it unconsciously and rising unconsciously, or doing both consciously [Horner 1966]. Oskar von Hinüber notes that the structural division into *vāras* and the technical term *samuṭṭhāna* connect the composition of the *Parivāra* methodologically with the *Nettippakaraṇa* [von Hinüber 1996].
